forensic_followup_not_part_of_official_t.interpretation: Two back-to-back real invocations of the exact same command in the exact same worktree produced different exit codes -- this is real flakiness/non-determinism in this environment, not a domain-model logic bug like the E-init-empty episode's mix.lock/ranch mismatch. The most plausible real cause, discovered from this episode's own isolation section above: a sibling agent was independently compiling/running against this SAME shared worktree during the exact window step 2 ran in (evidenced by the reappeared, differently-pid'd .qualification_server.log/.pid at 14:14, after step 2 had already started its ~157s run). Concurrent compilation or a concurrent mix test invocation contending for the same _build/test and deps/*/ebin directories is a concrete, plausible mechanism for a spurious first-run failure that clears on an uncontended re-run. This was NOT independently confirmed (e.g. by inspecting the sibling agent's own process for a timestamp overlap beyond the log/pid evidence already described), so it is reported as the most plausible explanation, not a proven one.
forensic_followup_not_part_of_official_t.why_this_is_not_used_to_overwrite_termin: The domain's own official actual_trajectory (step 2) is the one and only real run_tests invocation this episode's Ex4pmQualificationDomain instance actually attributes to itself. Substituting the second, out-of-band run's passing result into terminal_standing would be exactly the 'forcing a false green' the task instructed against for the control episode, applied here to a different but analogous temptation -- it is not done.
